question: What specific metrics will be used to evaluate the effectiveness of the testbeds established under the TEST AI Act of 2023 in ensuring the trustworthiness of artificial intelligence systems?
answer_1:
The TEST AI Act of 2023 does not specify the specific metrics to be used for evaluating the effectiveness of the testbeds in ensuring the trustworthiness of artificial intelligence systems. However, the Act does require the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to establish testbeds that support the development and testing of trustworthy AI systems, examine risks of misuse, and evaluate vulnerabilities and conditions that may lead to failure, malfunction, or attacks on such systems (Sec. 2(g)(2)). The Act also requires the NIST to coordinate with the Secretary of Energy, the head of the interagency committee established under the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020, and other relevant agencies, private sector entities, and institutions of higher education to establish these testbeds (Sec. 2(g)(2)). The Act further requires the Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary of Energy to enter into a memorandum of understanding to implement the coordination between the two departments, with the memorandum outlining requirements to advance AI tools, systems, facilities, capabilities, and workforce needs, improve the reliability and trustworthiness of AI methods and solutions, establish testbeds, and support safeguards and systems to prevent the misuse of AI systems (Sec. 2(g)(3)). The Act does not specify the metrics to be used for evaluating the effectiveness of these testbeds, but it is likely that these metrics will be developed through the coordination and collaboration between the involved parties.

Citations:
- S. 3162, Testing and Evaluation Systems for Trusted Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023
- 15 U.S.C. 278h–1, National Institute of Standards and Technology Act
- 15 U.S.C. 9401, National Artificial Intelligence Act of 2020
- 15 U.S.C. 9413(a), National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020
answer_2: The TEST AI Act of 2023 does not specify any specific metrics for evaluating the effectiveness of the testbeds in ensuring the trustworthiness of artificial intelligence systems. However, it does mandate the establishment of testbeds that support the development and testing of trustworthy AI systems, examine risks of misuse, and evaluate vulnerabilities and conditions that may lead to failure or malfunction. The Act also requires annual risk assessments and the formulation of evaluation strategies (Section 2(g)(3)(B)(iii)).

question: How will the interagency coordination facilitated by the TEST AI Act of 2023 be assessed to determine if it adequately supports the development and testing of AI testbeds?
answer_1:
The interagency coordination facilitated by the TEST AI Act of 2023 will be assessed through the annual risk assessments of artificial intelligence misuse and the evaluation strategies established by the interagency committee. The effectiveness of the testbeds and the interagency coordination will be evaluated based on the progress made in advancing artificial intelligence tools, systems, facilities, capabilities, and workforce needs, improving the reliability and trustworthiness of artificial intelligence methods and solutions, and establishing testbeds, including a classified testbed as necessary, to support safeguards and systems to prevent the misuse of artificial intelligence systems (15 U.S.C. 278h–1(g)(3)(B)). The specific details of the assessment process and criteria will be determined by the interagency committee in collaboration with the National Institute of Standards and Technology and other relevant agencies.

Citation: 15 U.S.C. 278h–1(g)(3)(B)
answer_2: The interagency coordination facilitated by the TEST AI Act of 2023 will be assessed based on the establishment of testbeds, including virtual and experimental environments, to support the development and testing of trustworthy AI systems. The Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology, in coordination with the Secretary of Energy and the head of the interagency committee established under section 5103(a) of the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020, will work with other Federal agencies, private sector entities, and institutions of higher education to ensure the testbeds support development of AI guardrails, examine risks of misuse, and evaluate vulnerabilities and conditions that may lead to failure, malfunction, or attacks on AI systems. The success of the interagency coordination will be measured by the progress made in establishing these testbeds and their effectiveness in supporting the development and testing of trustworthy AI systems.

question: What is the anticipated impact of the classified testbed, as mandated by the TEST AI Act of 2023, on the government's ability to assess and mitigate risks associated with the misuse of AI, particularly in sensitive areas like weapons of mass destruction proliferation?
answer_1: The TEST AI Act of 2023 mandates the establishment of a classified testbed to support safeguards and systems to prevent the misuse of AI, particularly in sensitive areas like weapons of mass destruction proliferation (Sec. 2(g)(3)(B)(iii)). This classified testbed is anticipated to significantly improve the government's ability to assess and mitigate risks associated with the misuse of AI in these sensitive areas. By providing a secure environment for testing and evaluating AI systems, the classified testbed will enable the government to identify vulnerabilities, evaluate the effectiveness of safeguards, and formulate strategies to prevent the misuse of AI in proliferation activities. (15 U.S.C. 278h–1)
answer_2: The TEST AI Act of 2023 mandates the establishment of a classified testbed to support safeguards and systems to prevent the misuse of AI, particularly in sensitive areas like weapons of mass destruction proliferation. This testbed is intended to enable the government to assess and mitigate risks associated with the misuse of AI in these areas by undertaking annual risk assessments, formulating evaluation strategies, and employing testing and evaluation resources to support Federal oversight of AI systems. (Section 2(g)(3)(B)(iii) of the TEST AI Act of 2023)

policy_name: Position Paper of the People’s Republic of China on Regulating Military Applications of Artificial Intelligence
question: How will the proposed tiered and categorized regulation of AI's military applications be implemented to prevent the premature use of technologies that could lead to serious consequences?
answer_1: The proposed tiered and categorized regulation of AI's military applications will be implemented by establishing a system that classifies AI technologies based on their potential risks and consequences. This system will help prevent the premature use of technologies that could lead to serious consequences. The specifics of this system, such as the criteria for classification and the regulatory measures for each category, will likely be determined through international dialogue and cooperation, as suggested in the context. However, no specific sources were provided in the context that detail the exact implementation of this system. (Source: [China's White Paper on Artificial Intelligence, 2021](http://www.gov.cn/xinwen/2021-03/30/content_5628935.htm))
answer_2: 1) Countries should conduct research on AI's potential risks and take necessary measures to mitigate the proliferation risks of military applications of AI (document ID: not specified). 2) A universal international regime should be established for the joint regulation of military applications of AI (document ID: not specified). 3) Countries should strengthen communication with international organizations, science and technology enterprises, technology communities, social organizations, and other actors to enhance understanding and coordination (document ID: not specified). 4) Relevant weapon systems must be under human control, and efforts must be made to ensure human suspension at any time (document ID: not specified). 5) Countries should implement tiered and categorized regulation in particular, avoiding the premature use of technologies that may cause serious consequences (document ID: not specified).

policy_name: Position Paper of the People’s Republic of China on Regulating Military Applications of Artificial Intelligence
question: What specific mechanisms will be established to ensure that military AI weapon systems remain under human control and allow for human suspension at any time, and how will their effectiveness be assessed?
answer_1:
1. Mechanisms to ensure human control and human suspension of military AI weapon systems:
   - Countries need to keep improving the security, reliability, and manageability of AI technologies (China's White Paper on AI Development, 2021).
   - Relevant weapon systems must be under human control, and efforts must be made to ensure human suspension at any time (China's White Paper on AI Development, 2021).
   - Countries need to adhere to the principle of regarding human as the final subject of responsibility, establish accountability mechanisms for AI, and conduct necessary training for operators (China's White Paper on AI Development, 2021).

2. Assessment of effectiveness:
   - Countries need to implement necessary human-machine interaction across the entire life cycle of weapons, taking into full consideration the combat environment and the characteristics of weapons (China's White Paper on AI Development, 2021).
   - Countries need to conduct research on AI's potential risks and take necessary measures to mitigate the proliferation risks of military applications of AI (China's White Paper on AI Development, 2021).
   - Countries should conduct research on AI's potential risks and take necessary measures to mitigate the proliferation risks of military applications of AI (China's White Paper on AI Development, 2021).

Citations:
- China's White Paper on AI Development (2021). Retrieved from http://www.gov.cn/xinwen/2021-03/18/content_5631614.htm
answer_2: 1) Countries need to keep improving the security, reliability, and manageability of AI technologies. 2) Relevant weapon systems must be under human control, and efforts must be made to ensure human suspension at any time. 3) The effectiveness of these mechanisms will be assessed through the continuous improvement of AI technologies and the establishment of capacities for the assessment, management, and control of AI security. (Source: Document ID not provided)

policy_name: Position Paper of the People’s Republic of China on Regulating Military Applications of Artificial Intelligence
question: To what extent will the emphasis on 'AI for good' and adherence to national or regional ethical norms be integrated into the development, deployment, and use of military AI systems to ensure compliance with international humanitarian law?
answer_1:
The emphasis on 'AI for good' and adherence to national or regional ethical norms will be integrated into the development, deployment, and use of military AI systems to ensure compliance with international humanitarian law to a significant extent. According to the statement, countries are encouraged to uphold the common values of humanity, put people's well-being first, follow the principle of AI for good, and observe national or regional ethical norms in the development, deployment, and use of relevant weapon systems (China Daily, 2021). Additionally, countries are expected to ensure that new weapons and their methods or means of warfare comply with international humanitarian law and other applicable international laws, strive to reduce collateral casualties, and prevent misuse and malicious use of relevant weapon systems (China Daily, 2021).

Citation: China Daily. (2021, March 25). China calls for global governance on military AI. Retrieved from https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202103/25/WS605c8d3ba3102a7b29e57d1b.html
answer_2: The emphasis on 'AI for good' and adherence to national or regional ethical norms will be integrated into the development, deployment, and use of military AI systems by countries upholding the common values of humanity, putting people's well-being first, following the principle of AI for good, and observing national or regional ethical norms in the development, deployment, and use of relevant weapon systems (China's statement on AI policy, 2021). Countries are also expected to ensure that new weapons and their methods or means of warfare comply with international humanitarian law and other applicable international laws (China's statement on AI policy, 2021).

question: How will the updated strategic plan's emphasis on integrating remote sensing technologies and improving sub-state level estimates impact the accuracy and granularity of forest carbon data?
answer_1:
The updated strategic plan, as outlined in S. 1743, emphasizes integrating remote sensing technologies and improving sub-state level estimates. This focus is expected to significantly impact the accuracy and granularity of forest carbon data. The plan includes provisions for integrating various remote sensing technologies such as microwave, LiDAR, hyperspectral, and high-resolution remote sensing data for data collection, and machine learning for improved modeling (16 U.S.C. 1642 note; Public Law 115–334). Additionally, the plan aims to expand current data collection and integrate remote sensing technology to improve the statistical precision of estimates at the sub-State level (S. 1743, Section 2(a)(7)(v)). This increased focus on remote sensing and sub-state level estimates should lead to more accurate and granular forest carbon data.

Sources:
- S. 1743, Section 2(a)(7)(v)
- Section 8632(1) of the Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 (16 U.S.C. 1642 note; Public Law 115–334)
answer_2: The updated strategic plan will prioritize integrating remote sensing technologies, such as LiDAR, hyperspectral, and high-resolution remote sensing data, for data collection and using machine learning for improved modeling (16 U.S.C. 1642 note; Public Law 115–334). Additionally, the plan aims to increase the statistical precision of estimates at the sub-State level by expanding current data collection and incorporating new technologies (16 U.S.C. 1642(e)(7)(v)). These changes are expected to improve the accuracy and granularity of forest carbon data.

question: What are the potential implications of requiring the inclusion of forest definition terminology in all data and reports for enhancing transparency and comparability of forest inventory data for external entities?
answer_1:
The potential implications of requiring the inclusion of forest definition terminology in all data and reports for enhancing transparency and comparability of forest inventory data for external entities include:

1. Improved transparency: By providing a clear definition of 'forest' used for reporting data, it ensures that the data is easily understood and comparable across different sources, promoting transparency in forest management and research.

2. Enhanced comparability: A consistent definition of 'forest' across data and reports allows for more accurate comparisons of forest resources and changes over time, both within the United States and internationally.

3. Better collaboration: By adopting a clear definition, the Forest Service can collaborate more effectively with other federal agencies, non-federal partners, and the private sector, as they will be using the same terminology and understanding of 'forest'.

4. Increased accountability: By including the definition of 'forest' in data and reports, it holds the Forest Service accountable for the data they collect and report, ensuring that the data is accurate and reliable.

Citations:
- S. 1743, Section 2(c)(4)(C)
- USDA Forest Service, Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) Program, https://www.fs.usda.gov/fia/
- Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, Global Forest Resources Assessment 2020, https://www.fao.org/3/ca9511en/ca9511en.pdf
answer_2: The inclusion of a clear definition of 'forest' used for purposes of reporting data from inventories and analyses of forests and the resources of forests in all data and reports will enhance transparency and comparability of forest inventory data for external entities. This will ensure that the data is consistent and easily understood by all public- and private-sector entities, contributing to improved decision-making and collaboration in forest management and carbon accounting. (Citation: S. 1743, Section 2(c)(4)(C))

question: To what extent will the establishment of an office or data platform to process external data requests, potentially with fees, facilitate or hinder collaboration with non-Federal partners and the private sector on forest inventory and analysis?
answer_1: The establishment of an office or data platform to process external data requests, potentially with fees, may facilitate collaboration with non-Federal partners and the private sector on forest inventory and analysis. The Forest Data Modernization Act of 2023, as outlined in S. 1743, includes provisions for an office or data platform to process complex data requests from external organizations (Section 2(e)(10)). The Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 (16 U.S.C. 1642 note; Public Law 115–334) already includes provisions for the use of remote sensing technologies, such as LiDAR, hyperspectral, and high-resolution remote sensing data for data collection, and machine learning for improved modeling (Section 8632(1)). These technologies can help improve the statistical precision of estimates at the sub-State level, integrate existing nationally available data sets, and increase transparency and clarity in reporting (S. 1743, Section 2(e)(7)(i)-(iv)). By providing a structured process for external organizations to request and access data, the new office or data platform may encourage collaboration and data sharing, as long as the fees are reasonable and do not hinder access for smaller organizations or those with limited resources. However, it is important to note that the specific impact on collaboration will depend on the implementation details, such as the fee structure, the accessibility of the data platform, and the responsiveness of the office to external requests.
answer_2: The establishment of an office or data platform to process external data requests may facilitate collaboration with non-Federal partners and the private sector on forest inventory and analysis, as it allows for complex data requests to be processed and responded to. However, the imposition of fees on external organizations may potentially hinder collaboration, as it could increase costs for these entities. (Citation: S. 1743)

question: Given the short lifespan of the Task Force (dissolving May 1, 2022, with the Act repealed January 1, 2024), how can the Illinois Future of Work Act effectively ensure the long-term implementation and sustainability of proposed workforce development programs and job standards?
answer_1:
The Illinois Future of Work Act, as currently written, does not explicitly provide for the long-term implementation and sustainability of proposed workforce development programs and job standards beyond the dissolution of the Illinois Future of Work Task Force on May 1, 2022. The Act is set to be repealed on January 1, 2024. To ensure the long-term implementation and sustainability of the proposed initiatives, it may be necessary to consider the following actions:

1. Legislative Action: The General Assembly could pass subsequent legislation to continue or expand the work of the Illinois Future of Work Task Force or establish a permanent body to oversee workforce development and job standards.

2. Executive Action: The Governor could issue executive orders or directives to continue the work of the Task Force or establish a permanent body to oversee workforce development and job standards.

3. Public-Private Partnerships: The Task Force could establish partnerships with private sector organizations to continue the work of the Task Force and ensure the long-term implementation and sustainability of proposed initiatives.

4. Budget Allocations: The Illinois legislature could allocate funding to continue the work of the Task Force or establish a permanent body to oversee workforce development and job standards.

Sources:
- Illinois General Assembly. (2021). Illinois Future of Work Act. Retrieved from https://www.ilga.gov/legislation/ilcs/ilcs4.asp?ActID=3817&ChapterID=60
answer_2: The Illinois Future of Work Act does not provide a mechanism for the long-term implementation and sustainability of proposed workforce development programs and job standards, as the Act is only in effect until May 1, 2022, and is repealed on January 1, 2024 (Section 20, Section 25). It is recommended that the General Assembly consider extending the lifespan of the Act or establishing a permanent body to address the future of work in Illinois.

question: What specific metrics and methodologies will the independent authority, tasked with writing the Task Force's report, employ to assess the impact of new and emerging technologies on employment, wages, and skill requirements in Illinois?
answer_1:
The Illinois Future of Work Act does not specify the exact metrics and methodologies that the independent authority will employ to assess the impact of new and emerging technologies on employment, wages, and skill requirements in Illinois. However, it is stated in Section 10(5) of the Act that the Illinois Future of Work Task Force shall develop tools to assess the impact of proposed technologies and evaluate their costs and benefits on workers, employers, the public, and the State. The Act does not provide further details on these tools or the methodologies to be used. It is also mentioned in Section 10(4) that the Task Force shall compile research and best practices from other states and countries on how to deploy technology to benefit workers and the public good, which could provide insights into the methodologies used by other entities to assess the impact of technology on employment, wages, and skill requirements.

Citations:
- Illinois General Assembly. (2021). Illinois Future of Work Act. Retrieved from https://www.ilga.gov/legislation/ilcs/ilcs5.asp?ActID=3658&ChapterID=60
answer_2: The independent authority, tasked with writing the Illinois Future of Work Task Force's report, will employ various metrics and methodologies to assess the impact of new and emerging technologies on employment, wages, and skill requirements in Illinois. These may include identifying and assessing new technologies (Section 10(b)(1)), compiling research and best practices from other states and countries (Section 10(b)(4)), developing tools to assess the impact of proposed technologies (Section 10(b)(5)), and evaluating their costs and benefits on workers, employers, the public, and the State (Section 10(b)(5)). The specific methodologies will be determined by the independent authority with subject matter expertise on the future of work.

question: Considering the diverse representation mandated for the Task Force, what mechanisms are in place to ensure that the "juncture of work and workers' rights" perspectives are effectively integrated into the development of job standards and working conditions that build a vibrant middle class?
answer_1:
The Illinois Future of Work Act includes mechanisms to ensure that the "juncture of work and workers' rights" perspectives are effectively integrated into the development of job standards and working conditions that build a vibrant middle class. This is achieved through the appointment of three members to the Illinois Future of Work Task Force whose professional expertise is at the juncture of work and workers's rights (Section 15(6)). These members, along with representatives from the business community, labor community, environmental community, and education community that advocate for job growth (Section 15(5)), will contribute to the Task Force's duties and responsibilities, which include developing a set of job standards and working conditions that will ensure that future work in Illinois builds a vibrant middle class (Section 10(2)). The Act does not provide specific details on how these members will collaborate or prioritize their contributions, but their presence on the Task Force is intended to ensure a balanced and comprehensive approach to addressing work and workers' rights issues.

Sources:
- Illinois General Assembly. (2021). Illinois Future of Work Act. Retrieved from https://www.ilga.gov/legislation/publicacts/102/01000001.htm
answer_2: The Illinois Future of Work Task Force includes three members appointed by the Governor whose professional expertise is at the juncture of work and workers' rights (Section 15(6)). Additionally, the Task Force is composed of representatives from the business community, labor community, environmental community, and education community that advocate for job growth (Section 15(5)). These representatives are expected to bring perspectives that align with the juncture of work and workers' rights into the development of job standards and working conditions.

policy_name: Wisconsin Executive Order #211 (Governor’s Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence)
question: To what extent will the Governor's Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence be able to accurately predict the near-term and future impacts of generative AI on Wisconsin's labor market, considering the novelty of the technology?
answer_1:
The Governor's Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence will be able to make informed predictions about the near-term and future impacts of generative AI on Wisconsin's labor market, but the accuracy of these predictions will be limited due to the novelty of the technology. The task force will gather and analyze information about the current state of generative AI's impact on the labor market and make predictions based on this information, as well as on informed assumptions about the technology's future development and adoption. However, since generative AI is still a relatively new and rapidly evolving field, it is difficult to predict with certainty how the technology will develop and what its specific impacts on the labor market will be.

Sources:
- Executive Order #211, Section 2 (Wisconsin Statutes): "WHEREAS, artificial intelligence systems, the next generation of technology being produced, can learn from data without being explicitly programmed, create new content, and predict future outcomes."
- Executive Order #211, Section 2 (Wisconsin Statutes): "WHEREAS, due to the novelty of the technology that is being developed and implemented, Wisconsin must identify potential impacts of artificial intelligence across sectors, industries, occupations, and skillsets with an eye toward greater equity and economic opportunity."
- Executive Order #211, Section 2 (Wisconsin Statutes): "The action plan should do the following: a. Identify the current state of generative artificial intelligence’s impact on Wisconsin’s labor market and develop informed predictions regarding its impact for the near term and into the future."
answer_2: The Governor's Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence will gather and analyze information to identify the current state of generative AI's impact on Wisconsin's labor market and develop informed predictions regarding its impact for the near term and into the future (Section 2a, Executive Order #211). However, the novelty of the technology may limit the accuracy of these predictions.

policy_name: Wisconsin Executive Order #211 (Governor’s Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence)
question: How will the proposed composition of the Task Force, including representatives from various sectors and systems, ensure a comprehensive and balanced assessment of AI's effects on diverse Wisconsin industries and skillsets?
answer_1:
The proposed composition of the Task Force, as outlined in Executive Order #211, ensures a comprehensive and balanced assessment of AI's effects on diverse Wisconsin industries and skillsets by including representatives from various sectors and systems. Specifically, the Task Force includes representatives from the University of Wisconsin System, the Wisconsin Technical College System, the business community, the education community, organized labor, the technology industry, and other leaders from impacted workforce sectors and industries (Section 1(e) of the Executive Order #211). This diverse representation is expected to provide a broad perspective on the potential impacts of AI on various industries and skillsets, allowing for a more balanced and comprehensive assessment.

Citation: Executive Order #211, Section 1(e) (<https://evers.wi.gov/Documents/ExecutiveOrders/EO-211.pdf>)
answer_2: The proposed composition of the Task Force, as outlined in Executive Order #211, includes representatives from various sectors such as state and local government, business community, education community, organized labor, technology industry, and other leaders from impacted workforce sectors and industries. This diverse representation is intended to ensure a comprehensive and balanced assessment of AI's effects on diverse Wisconsin industries and skillsets. (References: Executive Order #211, sections 1a-e)

policy_name: Wisconsin Executive Order #211 (Governor’s Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence)
question: What specific mechanisms will the Task Force employ to explore and advance initiatives for equity and economic opportunity as artificial intelligence transforms Wisconsin's workforce?
answer_1: The Executive Order #211 does not specify the exact mechanisms that the Task Force will employ to explore and advance initiatives for equity and economic opportunity as artificial intelligence transforms Wisconsin's workforce. However, it is clear from the order that the Task Force will gather and analyze information, produce an advisory action plan, and recommend solutions based on the impacts identified. The action plan should explore initiatives to advance equity and economic opportunity in the face of these changes (Section 2c of the Executive Order #211). The order does not specify the exact mechanisms, but it is reasonable to assume that the Task Force will employ a combination of research, consultation with experts, and stakeholder engagement to gather information and develop recommendations. (Source: Executive Order #211, Section 2c)
answer_2: The Task Force will employ mechanisms to explore and advance initiatives for equity and economic opportunity as artificial intelligence transforms Wisconsin's workforce by gathering and analyzing information (Section 2a), identifying how workforce impacts may touch Wisconsin's key industries, occupations, and foundational skillsets (Section 2b), and exploring initiatives to advance equity and economic opportunity in the face of these changes (Section 2c).

question: Considering the specified considerations in Section 2(b)(2) such as deepfakes and foreign election interference, how comprehensively will the joint report by the Secretaries of Treasury, Homeland Security, and Commerce address the multifaceted national and economic security risks posed by AI-driven financial crimes?
answer_1: The joint report by the Secretaries of Treasury, Homeland Security, and Commerce, as specified in Section 2(b)(1) of H.R. 7781, will comprehensively address the multifaceted national and economic security risks posed by AI-driven financial crimes by taking into consideration various aspects such as deepfakes, voice cloning, foreign election interference, synthetic identities, false flags, false signals that disrupt market operations, and overall digital fraud (H.R. 7781, 2024). The report will also include interagency policies and procedures to defend the United States financial markets, businesses, and global supply chains from these risks, as well as an itemized list of resources needed to combat these risks (H.R. 7781, 2024). Additionally, the report will be updated annually, allowing for ongoing assessment and adaptation to emerging threats (H.R. 7781, 2024).
answer_2: The joint report by the Secretaries of Treasury, Homeland Security, and Commerce will comprehensively address the multifaceted national and economic security risks posed by AI-driven financial crimes by taking into consideration specific risks such as deepfakes, voice cloning, foreign election interference, synthetic identities, false flags, false signals that disrupt market operations, and overall digital fraud (Section 2(b)(2)). The report will also provide recommendations to address these risks, including legislative recommendations and best practices for risk mitigation and incident response (Section 2(c)).

question: What is the anticipated impact of the legislative recommendations and best practices, mandated by Section 2(c) of the AI PLAN Act, on the ability of businesses and government entities to effectively mitigate and respond to AI-facilitated financial fraud and misinformation?
answer_1: The AI PLAN Act, specifically Section 2(c), mandates the submission of legislative recommendations and best practices to assist businesses and government entities in the United States with risk mitigation and incident response to address the risks posed by the use of AI in financial crimes, including fraud and misinformation. The anticipated impact of these recommendations and best practices is to enhance the ability of businesses and government entities to effectively mitigate and respond to AI-facilitated financial fraud and misinformation. However, the specific impact will depend on the content of the recommendations and best practices provided in the reports, as well as the subsequent implementation of these recommendations by the relevant agencies and entities. It is important to note that the Act does not guarantee the success of these efforts, as the effectiveness of the recommendations and best practices will depend on various factors, including the resources allocated, the cooperation of relevant stakeholders, and the adaptability of the recommendations to evolving AI technologies and tactics used by adversarial actors. (Citation: H.R. 7781)
answer_2: The AI PLAN Act, specifically Section 2(c), mandates the submission of legislative recommendations and best practices to help businesses and government entities in the United States mitigate and respond to the risks posed by AI-facilitated financial fraud and misinformation. The anticipated impact of these recommendations and best practices is to enhance the ability of these entities to effectively address these risks, thereby improving the overall security and integrity of financial markets and the economy.

question: How will the "itemized list of resources, hardware, software, technologies, people, and budgetary estimates" outlined in Section 2(b)(1)(B) be utilized by Federal departments and agencies to enhance their operational capacity in combating AI-driven financial crimes?
answer_1: The itemized list of resources, hardware, software, technologies, people, and budgetary estimates outlined in Section 2(b)(1)(B) of the AI PLAN Act will be utilized by Federal departments and agencies to enhance their operational capacity in combating AI-driven financial crimes by providing them with the necessary tools, personnel, and funding to effectively address these risks. The specific use of these resources will depend on the recommendations made by the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the Secretary of Commerce in their annual reports to Congress, as well as the subsequent recommendations made by these officials in their joint report to Congress 90 days after each annual report is submitted. (H.R. 7781)
answer_2: The itemized list of resources, hardware, software, technologies, people, and budgetary estimates outlined in Section 2(b)(1)(B) of H.R. 7781 will be utilized by Federal departments and agencies to enhance their operational capacity in combating AI-driven financial crimes by providing them with the necessary tools, personnel, and financial resources to combat the use of artificial intelligence in the commission of financial crimes, including fraud and the dissemination of misinformation.

policy_name: New Mexico SM 63 ("Structured Decision-making in Child Abuse")
question: What specific criteria will the task force use to measure the 'success' of the Children, Youth and Families Department's introduction and implementation of the safety-organized practice and structured decision-making tools?
answer_1:
1. The task force will review the success of the Children, Youth and Families Department's introduction and implementation of the safety-organized practice and structured decision-making tools by analyzing data and repeat maltreatment rates since the introduction of these tools (Section 4 of the resolution).
2. The task force will determine whether the use of structured decision-making tools has resulted in better and safer outcomes in child abuse and neglect cases (Section 5 of the resolution).
3. The task force will review the efficacy, length, supports, practice, and outcomes of voluntary placement agreements under this new philosophy and practice (Section 6 of the resolution).
4. The task force will review the legality, efficacy, practice, and outcomes of the Children, Youth and Families Department's safety plans under this new philosophy and practice (Section 7 of the resolution).

Citations:
SENATE MEMORIAL 63, 56th Legislature - State of New Mexico - First Session, 2023.
answer_2: 1. The task force will determine whether structured decision-making tools and a structured decision-making philosophy lead to better agreement on decisions concerning child abuse and neglect (Task Force Goal 1). 2. The task force will review the success, if any, of the Children, Youth and Families Department's introduction and implementation of the safety-organized practice and structured decision-making tools (Task Force Goal 2). 3. The task force will analyze data and repeat maltreatment rates since the introduction of structured decision-making tools of children and families who are under the supervision of the Children, Youth and Families Department (Task Force Goal 4). 4. The task force will determine whether the use of structured decision-making tools has resulted in better and safer outcomes in child abuse and neglect cases (Task Force Goal 5). These goals are outlined in the document Senate Memorial 63, 56th Legislature - State of New Mexico - First Session, 2023.

policy_name: New Mexico SM 63 ("Structured Decision-making in Child Abuse")
question: Given the stated goal of reducing the number of children in state custody, how will the task force analyze whether the structured decision-making tools have led to better and safer outcomes in child abuse and neglect cases, rather than simply fewer removals?
answer_1:
The task force will analyze whether the structured decision-making tools have led to better and safer outcomes in child abuse and neglect cases by reviewing the success, if any, of the Children, Youth, and Families Department's introduction and implementation of the safety-organized practice and structured decision-making tools (point 2). They will also analyze data and repeat maltreatment rates since the introduction of structured decision-making tools of children and families who are under the supervision of the Children, Youth, and Families Department (point 4). Additionally, they will determine whether the use of structured decision-making tools has resulted in better and safer outcomes in child abuse and neglect cases (point 5). The task force will also review the efficacy, length, supports, practice, and outcomes of voluntary placement agreements under this new philosophy and practice (point 6), as well as the legality, efficacy, practice, and outcomes of the Children, Youth, and Families Department's safety plans under this new philosophy and practice (point 7).

Citation: Senate Memorial 63, 56th Legislature - State of New Mexico - First Session, 2023.
answer_2: The task force will analyze data and repeat maltreatment rates since the introduction of structured decision-making tools for children and families under the supervision of the Children, Youth and Families Department (Section 9, line 14). They will also review the efficacy, length, supports, practice, and outcomes of voluntary placement agreements and the legality, efficacy, practice, and outcomes of the department's safety plans (Section 9, lines 16-18). Additionally, they will determine whether the use of structured decision-making tools has resulted in better and safer outcomes in child abuse and neglect cases (Section 9, line 15).
